Reading of the table:

  1. Among GWP100_{100} choices, the total moves only between 150 and 160 kt CO2_2e yr−1^{-1} (about ±3 % around the base case). The headline annual figure is therefore robust to the assessment-report choice, provided the horizon is 100 years and the basis is stated.
  2. The horizon is not a minor choice. On a 20-year horizon the same physical plant reports about 262–265 kt CO2_2e yr−1^{-1}, about 1.7 times the GWP100_{100} figure, and methane becomes the larger term. GWP20_{20} is not the convention for inventory reporting, but it is the relevant sensitivity for near-term climate effect, and the two figures must never be mixed or quoted without the horizon.
  3. Uncertainty in the leak rate itself acts linearly and is likely larger than the spread in item 1. If the true leak is 3 kt yr−1^{-1} rather than 2 kt yr−1^{-1} (a 50 % underestimate, within the range found when top-down atmospheric measurements are compared with bottom-up fugitive inventories at oil, gas, and chemical sites), the base-case total becomes 100 + 3 × 29.8 = 189.4 kt CO2_2e yr−1^{-1}, and the unallocated intensity becomes 2.37 t CO2_2e t−1^{-1}. A leak figure should therefore carry its measurement method (emission-factor estimate, component survey, or continuous/top-down measurement) with it.

Two data items would convert the bounded results above into single product-footprint figures: (i) the origin of the methane (fossil or non-fossil) and the reporting scheme's prescribed GWP set, which fixes the weighted total within the 150–160 kt CO2_2e yr−1^{-1} range; and (ii) the co-product quantity and the chosen allocation basis (or the displaced-production credit), which fixes fPf_P.

  • IPCC (2021). Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Contribution of Working Group I to the Sixth Assessment Report. Chapter 7, Table 7.15: GWP20_{20} and GWP100_{100} for CH4_4 of 82.5 and 29.8 (fossil) and 80.8 and 27.2 (non-fossil); GWP for CO2_2 = 1.
  • IPCC (2013). Climate Change 2013: The Physical Science Basis (Fifth Assessment Report): GWP100_{100} for CH4_4 = 28.
  • IPCC (2007). Climate Change 2007: The Physical Science Basis (Fourth Assessment Report): GWP100_{100} for CH4_4 = 25.
  • ISO 14044:2006. Environmental management — Life cycle assessment — Requirements and guidelines: allocation hierarchy (avoid allocation by subdivision or system expansion; then physical relationships; then other relationships, in practice economic value).

Response with defensive prompt

Annual Emissions and Product Carbon Intensity

Declared basis
Item Declaration
Standards Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard for the plant total; GHG Protocol Product Life Cycle Accounting and Reporting Standard and International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 14044 allocation hierarchy for the product intensity
Boundary Plant fence line, one operating year, direct emissions only (Scope 1 under the GHG Protocol). Included: direct carbon dioxide (CO₂) emission and fugitive methane (CH₄) leak. Excluded, for lack of data: purchased-energy emissions (Scope 2), upstream and downstream value-chain emissions (Scope 3), and all other greenhouse gases. No offsets or removals are deducted.
Consolidation approach Operational control is assumed; the problem states no equity share or financial-control boundary.
Allocation rule ISO 14044 hierarchy: allocation is avoided first by subdivision or system expansion; neither is possible with the data given, so allocation is used, as instructed. Two allocation bases are reported: mass (a physical relationship, preferred under the hierarchy) and economic value.
Horizons 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) as the primary reporting horizon, consistent with United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and Paris Agreement practice, and 20-year global warming potential (GWP20) as a sensitivity. Both horizons are reported throughout.
GWP values Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Sixth Assessment Report (AR6), fossil methane: GWP100 = 29.8 and GWP20 = 82.5, both dimensionless (kilogrammes of CO₂ equivalent per kilogramme of CH₄, kg CO₂e/kg CH₄). Carbon dioxide has GWP = 1 at every horizon by definition. The fossil values are used because a plant leak is treated here as fossil-origin methane; the non-fossil sensitivity is given in Section 3. If a reporting programme mandates AR5 or another GWP set, the totals change and must be restated.

This is therefore a direct-emissions (gate-to-gate, Scope 1 only) intensity. It is not a full cradle-to-gate or cradle-to-grave product carbon footprint, and it must not be reported as one.

Symbols and given data
  • ECO₂ = direct CO₂ emission rate = 100 kilotonnes per year (kt/yr), where 1 kt = 10⁶ kilogrammes (kg).
  • mCH₄ = methane leak rate = 2 kt CH₄/yr.
  • EH = total annual emission rate at horizon H, in kt of CO₂ equivalent per year (kt CO₂e/yr), where H is the GWP time horizon in years (yr), either 20 yr or 100 yr.
  • GWPH,CH₄ = global warming potential of methane at horizon H, dimensionless.
  • mp = principal product production rate = 80 kt/yr.
  • mc = co-product production rate, in kt/yr — not given.
  • pp = price of the principal product, in currency per tonne (t), and pc = price of the co-product, in currency per tonne — neither is given, and neither are the revenues.
  • f = allocation fraction, dimensionless: the share of EH assigned to the principal product.
  • IH = carbon intensity of the principal product at horizon H, in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent per tonne of principal product (t CO₂e/t), numerically equal to kilogrammes of CO₂ equivalent per kilogramme (kg CO₂e/kg).
1. Plant total annual emissions

The total at horizon H is

EH = ECO₂ + mCH₄ × GWPH,CH₄.

100-year horizon

  • Methane term: 2 kt CH₄/yr × 29.8 kg CO₂e/kg CH₄ = 59.6 kt CO₂e/yr.
  • Total: E₁₀₀ = 100 + 59.6 = 159.6 kt CO₂e/yr, reported as 160 kt CO₂e/yr at three significant figures.

20-year horizon

  • Methane term: 2 kt CH₄/yr × 82.5 kg CO₂e/kg CH₄ = 165.0 kt CO₂e/yr.
  • Total: E₂₀ = 100 + 165.0 = 265.0 kt CO₂e/yr, reported as 265 kt CO₂e/yr.
Horizon H CO₂ term (kt CO₂e/yr) CH₄ term (kt CO₂e/yr) Total EH (kt CO₂e/yr) CH₄ share of total
100 yr 100 59.6 159.6 37 %
20 yr 100 165.0 265.0 62 %

The mass emitted does not change with horizon; only the weighting of methane changes. Methane is 2 % of the emitted mass but 37 % of the GWP100 total and 62 % of the GWP20 total, so leak control is the largest single reduction lever at either horizon, and especially on a 20-year view.

2. Sensitivity to methane origin

If the leaked methane were non-fossil (biogenic) rather than fossil, the AR6 values would be GWP100 = 27.0 and GWP20 = 79.7, giving E₁₀₀ = 100 + 2 × 27.0 = 154.0 kt CO₂e/yr and E₂₀ = 100 + 2 × 79.7 = 259.4 kt CO₂e/yr. The origin of the methane is not stated in the problem; the fossil values in Section 1 are the stated basis, and this sensitivity bounds the effect of that choice (about 4 % at GWP100 and about 2 % at GWP20).

3. Carbon intensity of the principal product
3.1 Data limitation

A unique allocated intensity cannot be computed from the data given. Mass allocation requires mc, which is not given. Economic allocation requires pp, pc, and mc (or, equivalently, the two product revenues), none of which is given. Any single numerical allocated intensity would require inventing those values, so none is presented as a result. The exact results obtainable from the given data are (a) the unallocated intensity, which is the upper bound for the principal product, and (b) closed-form allocated intensities into which mc and the prices are inserted when known.

3.2 Unallocated intensity (all emissions to the principal product, f = 1)

IH = EH / mp.

  • GWP100: I₁₀₀ = 159.6 kt CO₂e/yr ÷ 80 kt/yr = 1.995 t CO₂e/t ≈ 2.00 t CO₂e/t (2.00 kg CO₂e/kg).
  • GWP20: I₂₀ = 265.0 kt CO₂e/yr ÷ 80 kt/yr = 3.3125 t CO₂e/t ≈ 3.31 t CO₂e/t (3.31 kg CO₂e/kg).
3.3 Mass allocation

The mass allocation fraction for the principal product is

fmass = mp / (mp + mc) = 80 / (80 + mc),

with mc in kt/yr. The allocated intensity is

IH,mass = EH × fmass / mp = EH / (80 + mc),

with EH in kt CO₂e/yr and the denominator in kt/yr, giving t CO₂e/t. That is:

  • GWP100: I₁₀₀,mass = 159.6 / (80 + mc) t CO₂e/t.
  • GWP20: I₂₀,mass = 265.0 / (80 + mc) t CO₂e/t.
3.4 Economic allocation

The economic allocation fraction for the principal product is the principal product's share of total product revenue:

fecon = (mp × pp) / (mp × pp + mc × pc) = (80 × pp) / (80 × pp + mc × pc).

The allocated intensity is

IH,econ = EH × fecon / mp = EH × fecon / 80,

giving:

  • GWP100: I₁₀₀,econ = 1.995 × fecon t CO₂e/t.
  • GWP20: I₂₀,econ = 3.3125 × fecon t CO₂e/t.
3.5 How any allocation result is read off

For either allocation basis, once its fraction f is known, the intensity is f times the unallocated value in Section 3.2. The table below is an arithmetic sensitivity only; the fractions shown are illustrative and are not data for this plant.

Allocation fraction f assigned to principal product I₁₀₀ (t CO₂e/t) I₂₀ (t CO₂e/t)
1.00 (no allocation; co-product assigned nothing) 2.00 3.31
0.80 (for example, mass allocation if mc were 20 kt/yr) 1.60 2.65
0.50 1.00 1.66

Mass and economic allocation give the same intensity only if the mass share and the revenue share happen to be equal. In general they differ: economic allocation shifts burden toward the higher-value product, so a high-priced principal product with a low-priced, heavy co-product receives a larger share under economic allocation than under mass allocation, and the reverse when the co-product carries most of the value.

4. Limitations and data required to complete the estimate
  1. Missing allocation data. mc, pp, and pc (or both revenues) are required before a single allocated intensity can be reported. Prices should be stated for a defined period (for example, a multi-year average), because economic allocation moves with market prices even when the process does not change.
  2. Partial boundary. Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions are excluded only because no data were supplied. A product carbon footprint under ISO 14067 or the GHG Protocol Product Standard requires the upstream (cradle-to-gate at minimum) inventory; the intensities here would rise if those emissions were included.
  3. Other gases and sources. Only CO₂ and CH₄ are included. Any nitrous oxide, fluorinated gases, or additional fugitive and process sources at the plant would add to EH.
  4. Uncertainty. No measurement uncertainty was supplied. Fugitive methane rates are typically the least certain term in such an inventory (often estimated from emission factors rather than measured), and the results are stated to three significant figures on the arithmetic only; that precision is not a statement of accuracy.
  5. GWP set. Results use IPCC AR6 fossil-methane values, as declared. A programme mandating a different assessment-report vintage changes the methane terms in Section 1 and every intensity in proportion.
5. Summary of reportable results
Quantity GWP100 basis GWP20 basis
Plant total, Scope 1 only 159.6 kt CO₂e/yr (≈ 160 kt CO₂e/yr) 265.0 kt CO₂e/yr
Principal-product intensity, unallocated (f = 1) 2.00 t CO₂e/t 3.31 t CO₂e/t
Principal-product intensity, mass allocation 159.6 / (80 + mc) t CO₂e/t 265.0 / (80 + mc) t CO₂e/t
Principal-product intensity, economic allocation 1.995 × fecon t CO₂e/t 3.3125 × fecon t CO₂e/t

where mc is the co-product rate in kt/yr and fecon is the principal product's revenue share as defined in Section 3.4. Numerical allocated intensities require those two inputs, which the problem does not supply.
